title: Credit Controller
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Credit Controller

Join a growing Credit Control team within an established and successful business, where you'll play an important role in supporting customers, resolving outstanding debt and managing credit risk. Following the implementation of a new business-wide system, the Credit Control function has expanded, creating an exciting opportunity for proactive Credit Controllers to join the team on a permanent basis.

About the Role

As a Credit Controller, you'll work closely with both internal teams and external customers to ensure outstanding debts are collected efficiently and invoice queries are resolved promptly. You'll also review credit limits in line with customer spend and risk, identify recurring issues and help implement effective solutions.

You'll be joining a highly supportive and collaborative Finance team, where colleagues work together to achieve shared goals and support one another through periods of change and increased activity.

Key Responsibilities
- Ensure outstanding debts are collected promptly when they fall due.
- Investigate and resolve invoice queries by liaising with internal teams and customers.
- Ensure appropriate resolutions are documented accurately.
- Identify and escalate high-risk customer accounts to management.
- Review accounts that have exceeded agreed credit limits and liaise with senior colleagues where appropriate.
- Identify recurring issues and disputes, recommend solutions and support their implementation.
- Maintain strong relationships with customers while providing a high standard of service.

Key Requirements
- Previous experience working within a Credit Control or Sales Ledger role.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Word.
- Strong time management, planning and organisational skills.
- Proactive and solutions-focused approach to problem-solving.
- Enthusiastic team player with a willingness to support colleagues.
- A customer-focused approach, with strong integrity and attention to detail.

What's on Offer
- Permanent opportunity within a supportive and collaborative Finance team.
- Bonus opportunity.
- Discounts, savings and cashback across numerous retailers.
- Life assurance.
- Enhanced family-friendly policies, including maternity, paternity and additional annual leave.
- Mental Health First Aiders and Employee Assistance Programme.
- Comprehensive induction and ongoing development opportunities.
- Financial education and access to financial support.
- Inclusive working environment where everyone is encouraged to be themselves.
- Opportunity to join a business investing in its people and long-term growth.

title: Finance Administrator (Payroll)
description:
Finance Administrator (Payroll)

Location: Burton Latimer, Northamptonshire
Hours: Monday Friday, 40 hours per week

About the Company

Our client is a third-generation, family-owned group of businesses with a proud 80-year history. Today, the Group employs over 150 people across multiple industries and continues to grow. Their head office, based in Burton Latimer, Northamptonshire, provides centralised support to six trading businesses throughout the UK, covering Finance, IT, HR, Health & Safety and Marketing.

Working with our client means joining a close-knit, people-focused organisation where employees are valued and supported. Despite operating across varied industries, each business within the Group shares a common culture of hard work, integrity and collaboration.

The Role

We re looking for a Finance Administrator with payroll experience to join the Group Finance team. This is a full-time, office-based position offering variety and the opportunity to support payroll and finance administration across several businesses within the Group.

Reporting to the Management Accountant, you ll help ensure payroll information is accurate, complete and processed on time. You ll be responsible for maintaining employee payroll records, processing payroll-related information, handling queries and supporting payroll reconciliations, alongside general finance and administrative duties.

This role would suit an organised and detail-focused individual with previous payroll experience who enjoys working with figures, meeting deadlines and supporting a busy finance function.

Key Responsibilities Payroll Administration
- Assist with the preparation and processing of payroll information, ensuring accuracy and deadlines are met.
- Maintain employee payroll records, ensuring information is accurate and up to date.
- Process new starter details, leavers, changes to pay and other employee amendments.
- Check timesheets, working hours, overtime, holiday, sickness and other payroll-related information.
- Assist with the calculation and processing of payroll adjustments, deductions and statutory payments, as required.
- Respond to payroll queries professionally and confidentially, liaising with employees, managers and external payroll providers where appropriate.
- Support payroll reconciliations and ensure payroll records agree with finance records.
- Maintain accurate payroll documentation and ensure sensitive employee information is handled confidentially.

Finance Administration
- Assist with payroll journals and related month-end processes.
- Support bank reconciliations and other routine finance administration.
- Assist with maintaining accurate financial records across the Group.
- Liaise with internal departments to resolve payroll and finance discrepancies.
- Provide general administrative support to the Finance team as required.

About You
- Previous experience in a payroll administration or payroll-focused finance role.
- Good working knowledge of payroll processes and employee payroll records.
- Strong IT skills, including Excel and Office 365.
- Experience using Sage 50 Payroll would be advantageous.
- Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach to work.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage deadlines and competing priorities.
- Good communication skills and the ability to handle confidential information appropriately.
- A proactive and reliable approach, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Experience working within a construction, manufacturing or multi-company environment would be beneficial.

What s on Offer?
- Competitive salary.
- 24 days annual leave plus 8 statutory bank holidays.
- Statutory pension contribution.
- On-site small gym.
- Ongoing training and career development opportunities within an established and growing business.

description:
Group Accounts Assistant

Location: Remote (preferred locations Northamptonshire/ Milton Keynes)

Hours: 25 hours per week (negotiable)

Salary: £30,000 pa, depending on experience

Join a growing team making a real impact

At Impact HR, and across our associated group companies, we are continuing to scale our operations and support to our client base.

To support this growth, we are recruiting for a Group Accounts Assistant who will be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day bookeeping and accounting of multiple companies within the business to support the Group Management Accountant.

This is a part-time role suited to a developing accounting professional who enjoys working in a growing SME environment and has the organisational skills to manage multiple entities. This role will progress bookkeeping skills with the complexity of supporting multiple companies within the group, with opportunities for the right candidate to develop further accounting skills.

Why this role matters

As the business grows, maintaining accuracy within Accounts Payable and Accounts Recievable of our various companies becomes increasingly important.

This role ensures the business maintains:
- Timely processing of Payable invoices
- Accurate delivery of Sales invoicing
- Monitoring of Aging debtors
- Responding to customer queries in a timely and professional manner

The Group Accounts Assistant will play an important role in supporting business leaders by ensuring the fundamentals of bookkeeping are accurate across the companies in their remit.

What you will be doing

You will be responsible for Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable of 3 companies, reporting to the Group Management Accountant.

This role oversees all core bookkeeping elements, with opportunities for accounting tasks and professional development.

Your day-to-day will include:

Within 3 of our companies:

Accounts Payable
- Processing and approving supplier invoices
- Reconciling bank account transactions
- Monitoring the Accounts mailboxes and responding to queries
- Maintaining and reviewing the fixed asset registers

Accounts Receivable
- Raising Sales invoices for 2-3 entities
- Chasing overdue invoices and resolving client invoice queries

What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months)
- Accurate and timely processing of purchase and sales invoices
- Well maintained bookkeeping records, fixed asset registers and bank reconciliations

About You

You are a developing accounting professional who enjoys working within a growing SME environment and is comfortable managing 3 Accounts mailboxes.

You bring strong attention to detail, initiative and a professional manner. You are comfortable asking questions when unsure.

You are organised, pragmatic and able to manage your workload effectively within a part-time role.

You will likely bring:
- 1+ years experience bookkeping or accounting
- Strong grades in Mathematics
- Ideally working towards an Accounting qualification such as AAT
- Accuracy and attention to detail
- Excellent prioritising and time management skills
- Proficiency with Outlook
- Experience using Accounting systems
- A solutions-focused mindset
- Application of data protection and confidentiality

What We Offer
- Competitive salary and benefits
- Flexible working
- Supportive, values-led team culture
- Progression pathways and professional development

Ready to shape the future of hr with Impact?

We are looking for a developing accounting professional who wants to play an important role in supporting a strong accounts foundation for a growing consultancy.

This role is about more than simply bookkeeping. It is about reliability, accuracy and adding value through solid accounting fundamentals, as well as requiring mental agility and organisation skills to manage multiple companies coherently. Once comfortable with the role, there are opportunities to develop various further accounting skills.

If you enjoy working in a flexible, collaborative environment and want the opportunity to apply your accounts expertise within a growing professional services organisation, we would love to hear from you.

description:
Part-Time Finance Officer (with Administrative Support)

JM&Co. Recruitment is working with an established local business looking to recruit an experienced and organised Part-Time Finance Officer to support its day-to-day financial operations and wider business administration.

This is a varied, hands-on position that would suit someone with a strong background in accounts or finance administration who enjoys taking ownership of their work, maintaining accurate financial records and supporting the smooth running of a business.

The role combines traditional accounts responsibilities with financial reporting and general administrative support, offering plenty of variety and the opportunity to become a valued part of the business.

Finance & Accounts

Maintaining accurate financial records, ledgers and accounting documentation.

Processing purchase and sales invoices, expenses, payments and receipts.

Managing accounts payable and receivable, including bank reconciliations.

Assisting with monthly management accounts and financial reporting.

Assisting with budgeting, forecasting and other financial activities.

Preparing reports, spreadsheets and other business documents.

Assisting with procurement, supplier management and related administration.

Supporting employee onboarding and general personnel administration.

Assisting with facilities administration, including tenant records, leases, insurance and site security arrangements.

Helping to maintain efficient and organised administrative processes.

About You

We are looking for someone with a good understanding of accounts and financial processes who is equally comfortable supporting wider administrative activities.

You will ideally have:

Previous experience in an accounts, bookkeeping, finance administration or similar position.

A sound understanding of accounting principles and day-to-day financial processes.

Experience using Xero accounting software.

Good Microsoft Excel skills and confidence using Microsoft Office.

Strong numerical ability with excellent accuracy and attention to detail.

Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.

A proactive, practical approach and the confidence to work independently.

Good written and verbal communication skills.

A professional and discreet approach when handling confidential information.

Desirable, but not essential:

An AAT qualification or equivalent accounting experience.

Experience assisting with payroll, VAT returns or management accounts.

Previous experience working within an SME or multi-business environment.

Knowledge of UK finance and employment administration requirements.

Working Hours & Salary

This is a permanent, part-time position offering approximately hours per week, depending on the successful candidate and the requirements of the business.

Salary will be dependent on experience and the skills the successful candidate can bring to the position, with flexibility for those offering particularly relevant experience.

The Part-Time Finance Officer Opportunity

This is an excellent opportunity for someone seeking a varied and responsible part-time role where they can put their finance experience to good use while supporting other areas of business administration.

It would particularly suit an experienced Accounts Assistant, Bookkeeper, Finance Administrator or Finance Officer looking for their next opportunity within a local business.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Payroll Assistant

Location: Pitsford, Northamptonshire (Office Based)
Salary: 26,000- 35,000 (doe) + quarterly, target based bonus

About the role

We're recruiting on behalf of a modern, forward-thinking accountancy practice that's built its reputation on providing exceptional service to a diverse portfolio of clients across Northamptonshire and beyond.

This isn't your typical accountancy firm.

They've invested heavily in technology, developed a genuinely supportive team culture and continue to grow through the quality of their service and client relationships. You'll be joining a business where your expertise is valued, your development is encouraged and your contribution genuinely makes a difference.

What You'll Be Doing
- Processing weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly and monthly payrolls for multiple clients
- Managing payrolls from start to finish with complete accuracy
- Calculating starters, leavers, overtime, commission, bonuses and deductions
- Processing statutory payments including SSP, SMP, SPP and ShPP
- Producing payslips, payroll reports and payment summaries
- Submitting FPS and EPS returns to HMRC
- Managing pension auto-enrolment duties and contribution uploads
- Processing tax code changes, student loans and attachment of earnings orders
- Preparing year-end payroll documentation including P45s and P60s
- Acting as a key point of contact for payroll-related client queries
- Liaising with HMRC and pension providers when required
- Setting up new payroll clients and onboarding employees
- Managing your own payroll calendar and ensuring all deadlines are met
- Supporting colleagues across the wider payroll team during busy periods

Who We're Looking For
- Has at least 5 years' payroll experience
- Has experience managing multiple client payrolls simultaneously
- Possesses strong knowledge of PAYE, RTI, NIC and statutory payments
- Is confident using payroll software such as BrightPay, Sage or Xero Payroll
- Has excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Can comfortably work to strict payroll deadlines
- Communicates professionally and confidently with clients
- Handles confidential information with discretion and professionalism
- Enjoys being part of a collaborative, client-focused team

Desirable:
